claims.text: The initial nanoparticles contain five metals in equal atomic ratios and form a single-phase FCC solid solution at room temperature.
Structural and chemical stability from 473 to 1923 K is governed by the balance between configurational entropy and mixing enthalpy.
The Gibbs free energy of mixing is given by ΔGmix = ΔHmix − TΔSmix.
Nanoparticles with average ΔHmix near 0 kJ/mol maintain negative ΔGmix and remain single-phase to higher temperatures.
Nanoparticles with strongly negative average ΔHmix undergo positive ΔGmix below approximately 1000 K.
Positive ΔGmix in the strongly negative-ΔHmix composition drives phase separation and elemental exsolution.
Replacing one element can produce Composition A with average ΔHmix near 0 kJ/mol and Composition B with average ΔHmix near −5 kJ/mol.
Gibbs free energy of mixing mediates the effect of composition on structural stability.
The critical temperature is approximately Tc = ΔHmix/ΔSmix.
Above the critical temperature, configurational entropy dominates and maintains a single-phase alloy.
Below the critical temperature, enthalpic driving forces cause phase decomposition and segregation.
Composition A will remain a single-phase solid solution up to at least 1800 K.
Composition A will exhibit no new XRD peaks and will retain spatially uniform EDS maps.
Composition B will develop new XRD phase peaks and elemental segregation at 900–1100 K.
Both Composition A and Composition B are single-phase FCC solid solutions at room temperature before thermal cycling.
The prediction applies under inert-atmosphere cycling to alloys with ΔSmix of approximately 1.5–1.7 R and average ΔHmix within ±10 kJ/mol.
The critical-temperature estimate has an uncertainty of ±200 K because of errors in ΔHmix and ΔSmix.
Identical stability profiles, or Composition B remaining single-phase to a temperature equal to or higher than Composition A, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated equation ΔGmix = ΔHmix − TΔSmix is inconsistent with the claim that a strongly negative ΔHmix and positive configurational entropy produce ΔGmix > 0 below about 1000 K. Under the stated equation, both terms make ΔGmix negative.
For Composition B, ΔHmix ≈ −5 kJ/mol and ΔSmix ≈ 1.5–1.7 R make the stated Tc ≈ ΔHmix/ΔSmix negative, not a positive critical temperature near 1000 K.

Composition B is asserted to be a single-phase FCC solid solution at room temperature, while the mechanism says it decomposes below a roughly 1000 K critical temperature. This could only be reconciled by an unstated kinetic or metastability argument.
